extracted.intended_audience: individuals applying for registration to practice before the USPTO; attorneys seeking review/remedies from the USPTO Director; counsel handling OED enrollment/discipline matters
extracted.subtask_description: Filing and litigating a petition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.3 to suspend USPTO rules and seeking remand/reconsideration of an OED Director denial of registration for lack of good moral character, including related timeliness, filing-method, and evidentiary issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary-situation requirement for rule suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may seek suspension of the rules "[i]n an extraordinary situation." 37 C.F.R. § 11.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain waiver/suspension under § 11.3 the petitioner must demonstrate extraordinary circumstances and that justice requires waiver. Allegations such as later admission to another bar, inability to complete the record, asserted substantive errors in the OED decision, or lack of alternative recourse do not automatically constitute an "extraordinary situation." The ordinary rule is that waiver is warranted only in truly extraordinary cases; the cited petition was denied because the petitioner did not meet this high standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of petitions/appeals (37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal/petition to the USPTO Director under 37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d) must be filed within sixty days of the mailing date of the OED Director's decision; requests for reconsideration must be filed within thirty days after the mailing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions not filed within the 60-day period are dismissed as untimely. The decision treats timeliness as jurisdictional and bars consideration of late appeals; the petitioner's December 18, 2007 appeal was dismissed as untimely and that dismissal foreclosed further relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee accompaniment requirement for appeals (37 C.F.R. and 1.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal under 37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d) must be accompanied by the appropriate fee as prescribed in the fee regulations (e.g., 37 C.F.R. 1.21(a)(5)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include the required fee (or meet the filing specifications) can be a basis for dismissal; petitions seeking suspension of the fee requirement must overcome the extraordinary-situation standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-new-evidence rule on Director review/reconsideration (37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will not consider new evidence in review of the OED Director's decision or upon reconsideration under § 11.2(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence that was not presented within the proper period (e.g., evidence arising after the OED decision or after the deadline for appeal/reconsideration) is properly excluded as 'new' and will not be considered. The petitioner’s State Bar admission, occurring after the relevant deadlines, was excluded under this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof to establish good moral character and reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for registration must demonstrate to the satisfaction of the OED Director that they possess good moral character and reputation as required to represent applicants before the USPTO (statutory and regulatory authority: 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D); 37 C.F.R. § 11.7(a)(2)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant carries the burden to create a record showing good moral character; the OED Director investigates and weighs the record. Applicants who fail to meet this burden may be denied registration; subsequent evidence presented late does not satisfy the burden for an earlier proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors supporting a finding against good moral character
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may base a finding that an applicant lacks good moral character on lack of candor, inconsistent statements, repeated charges/offenses, criminal convictions, violations of probation, and similar conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision emphasizes that the OED Director's determination rested on the whole record (lack of candor, inconsistent statements, multiple charges and offenses, violation of probation), and not on any single alleged error. Isolated clerical or wording errors (e.g., use of 'convictions' plural) are not dispositive if the record overall supports the adverse finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction-specific bar determinations are not dispositive
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination by one bar (e.g., State Bar of California) that an individual possesses good moral character does not automatically override a different agency's or jurisdiction's adverse finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bar admissions and character determinations are fact-specific and may differ across jurisdictions; it is not an extraordinary situation merely because one jurisdiction later admits the person while another previously denied admission. Agencies may accord differing weight to inconsistent statements that were part of the record before them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to complete the record and the applicant's duty to act timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are afforded the opportunity to complete the record (e.g., via Show Cause Requirement); however, they must timely submit and address inconsistencies and evidence. Failure to timely act (delays, missed appeals) can forfeit the opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED can issue a Show Cause Requirement when background disclosures (e.g., affirmative answers to application questions) raise issues; applicants who delay or fail to timely supplement the record cannot later claim lack of opportunity as grounds for extraordinary relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing method and date-of-receipt rules for facsimiles and originals (37 C.F.R. § 1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facsimile transmissions are accorded the date of receipt when the complete transmission is received (37 C.F.R. § 1.6(a)(3)), but facsimile submissions of matters requiring an original signature will not be accorded a date of receipt (37 C.F.R. § 1.6(d)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents requiring original signatures must be filed in a manner that satisfies the signature requirement to obtain an official date of receipt. Petitions seeking to suspend these rules must show extraordinary circumstances; simple reliance on faxing where originals are required is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of Director's decision on reconsideration (37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director's decision on reconsideration is the final agency action under § 11.2(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the Director issues a decision on reconsideration, that constitutes the final agency action and further petitions raising the same issues are barred unless they meet extraordinary-situation standards for rule suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of reapplication after denial (37 C.F.R. § 11.7(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual denied registration may reapply for registration two years after the date of the decision, unless a shorter period is ordered by the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reapplication must be accompanied by the appropriate fees (e.g., per 37 C.F.R. 1.21). The existence of the reapplication remedy weighs against finding that the petitioner lacks reasonable alternative recourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency rulemaking authority over recognition and conduct of practitioners (statutory authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO is authorized by federal law (35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D)) to promulgate rules and regulations governing the recognition and conduct of attorneys that practice before it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This authority supports the agency's promulgation and enforcement of its registration, filing, and evidentiary rules; petitioners cannot lightly ask the Director to waive those rules without satisfying the high § 11.3 standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality of alleged errors in OED decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged errors in the OED Director's decision (e.g., wording errors, plurality/terminology mistakes) must be material to the outcome to justify extraordinary relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor or non-outcome-determinative errors do not justify waiving procedural rules or remanding for reconsideration when the adverse decision is supported by the record as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show Cause Requirement when applicant gives affirmative background responses
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant gives an affirmative response to background or character questions, the OED Director may issue a Show Cause Requirement to give the applicant an opportunity to create a record addressing why registration should not be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Show Cause Requirement is the mechanism by which the OED gathers evidence concerning moral character and gives notice and opportunity to respond; failure to address issues raised by the Show Cause in a timely manner undermines later challenges.
